claim: OpenRouter official docs (fetched 2026-07-04): OpenRouter does not store prompts/responses by default; prompt retention is opt-in, while request metadata is stored. Provider-level logging/training is separate: OpenRouter reflects provider data policies per endpoint and gives users deny controls for providers that may collect or train, with separate account settings for paid vs free models. Zero Data Retention (ZDR) is enforceable globally, per model group, and per request; an unknown provider policy is conservatively treated as retain-and-train. For qwen/qwen3-coder:free and nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free the official model pages/API confirm free price, model slugs, and metadata, but the fetched pages/API exposed no per-endpoint data-policy tag, so the specific prompt-logging/retention/training status of those exact endpoints is UNVERIFIED from accessible official text. Free-tier rate limits: the official limits page states :free variants have per-minute and per-day limits, but the fetched text omitted the numeric values; the commonly cited 20 RPM and 50 requests/day without $10 purchased credits (1000/day with $10+) are UNVERIFIED from fetched official text, and whether failed attempts count into the quota is UNVERIFIED. If an account-level privacy setting denies free-model data collection/training, routes that do not match the privacy settings ERROR rather than complete.
